messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 downstream latency spike detected for hosted inference (eu-west2 -> eu-west3 cross-zone egress). Metric: streaming_tail_p99 = 2.8s (baseline 0.4s). Errors rising: TLS handshake timeouts and aborted streams. Alert ID: IB-1798754321.

alice-ops: seeing the same in the dashboard. Several customer routes showing +3s tail. Streaming stalls (clients report partial tokens then pause).

ben-oncall: ack. I'm paged and logging in. Starting quick impact check — which customers affected?

eve-cs: @ben-oncall two enterprise customers flagged unhappy: AcmeCorp chat integrations and Kapture.ai embedding pipelines. Both reported partial responses.

ben-oncall: thanks. @carla-net can you confirm if this looks like NAT/egress hotspots or something else?

carla-net: checking VPC egress metrics now. Early signs: NAT gateway ephemeral port exhaustion in eu-west2 for cross-zone flows. Conntrack metrics showing sharp rise.

carla-net: `conntrack_count_total` jumped from ~45k to 180k in ~3m; conntrack table nearing max on a subset of hosts. Also seeing elevated TCP retransmits and TLS handshake retries.

alice-ops: interesting — any recent deploys or routing changes in the last hour?

frank-devex: no deploys to runtime in last 2 hours per deploy-bot. Only a config rollout to weighted routing for model-fallback at 09:12, unlikely related.

ben-oncall: ok prioritize: 1) mitigate customer impact now, 2) confirm root cause (conntrack/NAT), 3) long-term fix. I'll run failover plan.

ben-oncall: mitigation attempt 1: shift a portion of traffic off eu-west2 egress to eu-west1 for streaming routes. Triggering routing override for high-latency routes. Command: `rbctl route override --route streaming --from eu-west2 --to eu-west1 --pct 30`

incident-bot: ACTION: route override applied (30%). Observed initial drop in p99 to ~1.2s for affected routes. Partial customer recovery for AcmeCorp.

carla-net: routing reduce helped but not enough. Conntrack still high on some worker pools because existing flows persist. We should recycle NAT agents on impacted subnets to free ephemeral ports.

alice-ops: agree. Plan: drain and restart nat-agent on two hosts in the affected AZ, sequentially. That will free conntrack entries. Do we have control plane downtime risk? Minimal for streaming; we'll drain by weight.

ben-oncall: proceed. I'll coordinate.

carla-net: starting drain on nat-agent-zt4 (az-b subset). Command run: `kubectl -n infra cordon nat-agent-zt4 && kubectl -n infra rollout restart ds/nat-agent -l az=zt4`

carla-net: restart done. Observing conntrack drop on that host from 60k -> 4k in ~45s. TLS handshake failures for clients routed through that host cleared.

frank-devex: note: streaming SDK will reconnect and resume if handshake succeeds. We should communicate to CS to tell customers short blip recovery.

eve-cs: messaging update: "We've mitigated an egress routing issue causing partial streaming stalls; engineers performed targeted restarts and reroutes. We're monitoring and will follow up." Sending now to AcmeCorp support contact.

ben-oncall: mitigation successful for ~70% of traffic; p99 back down to ~0.6-0.9s for many routes. However one worker pool still high.

carla-net: investigating the stubborn pool — it's a legacy subnet where NAT agent had a heavy outbound burst (port scanning from a customer misconfig?). Looking at flow logs.

alice-ops: can we temporarily expand ephemeral port range on the NAT gateway hosts to buy time? Sysctl tweak available: `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 1024 65535` — current min is 32768. But changing on prod hosts risks client compatibility; prefer restarts.

carla-net: agree restarts safer. Doing sequential restarts on remaining 3 hosts now.

incident-bot: PAGING: second oncall rotation needed for handoff in 18m. Current owner: ben-oncall. Please add notes to the incident channel for handoff.

ben-oncall: noted. After we finish restarts, I'll create a handoff message with runbook links and actions.

carla-net: all remaining restarts completed. Conntrack normalized cluster-wide. p95/p99 and streaming tail look stable on dashboards.

ben-oncall: monitoring for 20m. Customer-facing update: sent to AcmeCorp and Kapture.ai that we performed targeted network restarts and partial reroute; recovery in progress.

frank-devex: small follow-up: consider adding a streaming fallback in client SDK to reduce concurrent long-lived connections per device to avoid conntrack pressure. Filing a ticket: DEVEX-4123.

alice-ops: root cause hypothesis: sudden surge of short-lived concurrent outbound connections from a subset of tenants causing conntrack table blowout on NAT agents -> TCP retransmits -> TLS handshake stalls -> streaming stalls.

daniel-sre: agreed. Long-term actions I propose: 1) increase conntrack table size with safe guardrails for nat-agent, 2) implement per-tenant egress rate limiting and circuit-breakers, 3) add proactive conntrack alert (rate of new flows per host), 4) run chaos test for conntrack exhaustion.

ben-oncall: creating incident doc & follow-up tasks. Runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/network-conntrack-egress>. I'll include timeline, graphs, and customer impact notes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: IB-1798754321 mitigated at 1798754465. Severity downgraded to advisory. Please add postmortem owner and ETA.

eve-cs: requesting prioritized postmortem; customers want RCA and action plan. Assign to daniel-sre as PM?

daniel-sre: I'll own the postmortem. ETA: draft in 48 hours. Assigning follow-ups now: NAT config change task (INFRA-718), per-tenant egress limits (SEC-290), SDK reconnect/backoff design (DEVEX-4123).

ben-oncall: handing off monitoring to night oncall @frank-devex in 18m. Key notes in #incidents pinned: mitigation steps, runbook link, customer contacts, current metrics snapshot.

frank-devex: ack. Watching dashboards and will escalate if p99 > 1.2s for >5m.

alice-ops: final note — we should add synthetic streaming probes that exercise cross-zone egress to catch this earlier. Filing a task: SRE-909.

ben-oncall: thanks everyone. Closing active paging. Will post full timeline in the incident doc once draft is ready. :white_check_mark:

frank-devex: thanks team.
